title: Teton Dam failure: internal erosion, foundation key trench, rapid breach, and dam-safety memory
summary: Teton is encoded as a water-impoundment failure where internal erosion/piping in the foundation/core interface rapidly destroyed the dam during first filling, with consequence and memory surfaces kept separate from mechanism.

status_history.note: Added as rev0026 impoundment/tailings failure lane record.

subjects.name: Independent Panel to Review Cause of Teton Dam Failure

claims.claim: The Bureau of Reclamation Teton history page links both the 1976 Independent Panel report and the 1980 Department of the Interior final report on the failure.
what_would_change_status: A second-pass source review materially revises the extraction, narrows its scope, or adds a stronger primary source.

claims.claim: ASDSO’s case listing records that the Teton Dam failed on June 5, 1976, with 11 deaths and more than $1 billion in property damage.
what_would_change_status: A second-pass source review materially revises the extraction, narrows its scope, or adds a stronger primary source.

claims.claim: The ASDSO abstract of the Independent Panel report says the dam failed by internal erosion/piping of the core deep in the right foundation key trench, with eroded particles exiting through channels and along interfaces to the right groin.
what_would_change_status: A second-pass source review materially revises the extraction, narrows its scope, or adds a stronger primary source.

claims.claim: The same abstract says the design did not adequately account for foundation conditions and the fill characteristics in the key trench, while construction activities substantially conformed to the actual design except for scheduling.
what_would_change_status: A second-pass source review materially revises the extraction, narrows its scope, or adds a stronger primary source.

sequence_of_events: Initial filling; seepage/internal erosion developed in or near the core and foundation key trench; exit paths formed through rock joints/interfaces; breach progressed rapidly once piping was established.
type_payload.proximate_cause: internal erosion / piping through core-foundation interface
contributing_factors: design did not adequately account for foundation conditions
rapid breach evolution during first filling
latent_conditions: material-state and foundation complexity not legible enough in design/review surface
limited first-pass extraction of warning/evacuation chronology
historic consequence data needs second-pass official report extraction

handling_notes: Preserve casualty and community dignity; avoid spectacle and avoid using disasters as clever engineering anecdotes.
Separate physical mechanism, design/construction/operation history, monitoring or warning limits, regulatory/governance context, and post-event correction rails.
This record is historical/evidentiary infrastructure, not current engineering, mining, dam-safety, legal, or emergency-management advice.

unknowns: Direct report PDFs should be retrieved locally and hash-archived; current source extraction relies on report-index page and ASDSO abstract.
